$comment: Topic scoring. Weights are deliberately visible: the shortlist prints the formula and every input, so a ranking can be argued with. Change a weight here, never inside a candidate.

weights.$comment: score = Σ (component × weight). demand/speaker/effort/recency are computed by code; fit/pull are declared on the candidate and must carry their own evidence.

speaker_points.$comment: The real bottleneck is never ideas, it is a person willing to stand up. status values allowed on candidate.speaker.status.

effort_points.$comment: Negative = costs more to run. A workshop needs laptops, a bigger room and a second helper; on 2026-09-17 a plain talk in a library room took one organiser.

recency.$comment: A topic too close to one already delivered gets penalised: -5 if a past event's topic/title shares >= min_overlap keywords within window_months, scaled down with age.

evidence.$comment: Same rule as post-event numbers: a claim with no traceable source is not evidence. A ref is '<event-slug>:<path-into-results>', e.g. '2026-09-17-agent-security-ke-he:qa_questions[3].q'. Grade A = resolves and its results block carries checked+source; B = resolves, no provenance metadata on the block (qa_questions, feedback, observations); D = free text that resolves to nothing.
evidence.unranked_section_title: 未验证 —— 先去找证据，再谈排序

shortlist.$comment: How many candidates the generated shortlist recommends before the rest are listed as the long tail.

audience_profile_source.$comment: Which results keys describe who actually shows up / reads. The shortlist prints these so a topic is judged against the real audience, not an imagined one.
